chapter: Maynard Ferguson and Dizzy's big band
title: Leaving Ferguson for Dizzy's big band
summary: He joined Dizzy's big band with Benny Golson, Lee Morgan, Wynton Kelly and Melba Liston, learning a lot.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: He’s a monster player. Why’d you leave Maynard Ferguson?
Because I had an opportunity to go with Dizzy, I think.

Yeah, with Dizzy’s big band. That band was way over my head, but I had to go there anyway. Benny Golson was there, and Lee Morgan, Wynton Kelly. Melba Liston was the musical director. I had to go there. I had to go there and get kicked, kicked and beat-up on. I did it. They taught me a lot in there.
How long were you with Dizzy in its first incarnation?
About over a year, almost two years, something like that.
What was the touring and performance life of that aggregation during the time you were there?

Wonderful. Dizzy was very popular, and he was at a peak playing the trumpet. He paid more money than the other bands. He had a lot of respect for musicians and loved music dearly. He wrote wonderful arrangements himself. Then he had all the guys that could write on that level that he was writing on. I didn’t write anything for them.
